# generator-shortcuts — exact answer and runnable check

The strongest simple rival for the canonical demonstrations is **crop the
bounding box of every nonzero cell**, without assigning any special role to
color 9. It matches all three usable canonical pairs because their other
content lies inside the marker box. A row-only or column-only crop does not
fit those demonstrations and should not be presented as a canonical-fitting
rival merely because it worked on the old generated panels.

## An exact disagreeing input

Input: **3 rows × 4 columns**. Racket output: **2 rows × 2 columns**.

```json
[[2,0,0,2],
 [0,9,9,0],
 [0,9,0,0]]
```

The intended all-9 bounding box is rows 1..2 and columns 1..2, zero-based.
Actual selected canonical Racket output:

```json
[[9,9],
 [9,0]]
```

The all-nonzero rival returns the complete **3 rows × 4 columns** input, because
the two 2s extend the occupied rectangle to row 0 and both outside columns.
Two less obvious canonical-fitting rivals also disagree here: select the
least-frequent repeated color or the least-frequent even-count color (ties
favor the larger color), then crop that color's box. Both select the two 2s
and return **1 row × 4 columns**:

```json
[[2,0,0,2]]
```

The final validator accepts this input. `checks/shortcuts-v302/report.json`
retains the full public `Catalog.apply(reference="canonical",
allow_unapproved=True, check_generator_domain=True)` receipt, the input, actual
output and all rival outputs on final generator SHA-256
`dc6d9c68d1fb740b525c19716e9766060b8bf959585dcfd49b6634b08ebc9876`.
The executed rule hash is `a489a823697d` and matches the catalog. This is an
actual reference execution, not a guessed output from the generator or a
Python-only mirror.

## Does the proposed generator emit these counterexamples?

It does not emit this exact tiny grid: its construction canvas starts at 6×6,
while its validator intentionally accepts smaller lawful inputs. It **does**
emit the relevant disagreements naturally. In the final Racket-labeled probe,
seed 17, indices 0..11, each of easy/medium/hard, with no overrides:

| Rival | Canonical matches / 3 | Generated matches / 36 | Generated disagreements / 36 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All-nonzero crop | 3 | 0 | 36 |
| First/last row-major marker crop | 3 | 18 | 18 |
| Most-frequent nonzero-color crop | 3 | 18 | 18 |
| Least-frequent repeated-color crop | 3 | 18 | 18 |
| Least-frequent even-count-color crop | 3 | 18 | 18 |
| Second-most-frequent nonzero-color crop | 0 | 3 | 33 |
| Marker columns only | 0 | 0 | 36 |
| Marker rows only | 0 | 0 | 36 |
| Markers only inside the crop | 0 | 0 | 36 |

The first generated all-nonzero counterexample is easy/index 0; the first
generated first/last-marker, most-frequency, least-repeated and least-even
counterexamples are easy/index 1. Their full grids, Racket outputs, rival
outputs and source/seed bindings are retained in the report. All 40 checked
inputs pass the final validator, all five canonical-shortcut claims fit all
canonical pairs, and all nine competitors have generated refutations.

Run the included tool from `WORK`, using a new output filename:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 \
  generators/9c3781759581/workspace/probe_shortcuts.py \
  --out ../checks/shortcuts-new/report.json
```

The actual executed interpreter/argv and exit 0 are in
`checks/shortcuts-v302/command.json`. The tool reads the current declaration
registries rather than maintaining a second hard-coded rival-name list. The
positive-refutation regressions and larger period/rotation censuses are separate
evidence for complete lessons. All conclusions remain limited to the stated
rules, sources and finite checks.
